title: Seeded crispbreads
subtitle: thin, crisp seed-studded flatbreads made without yeast
excerpt: Seeded crispbreads are thin, cracker-like flatbreads made with flour, seeds, oil, and water, rolled as thin as possible and baked until completely crisp. There is no yeast; the thinness and the seeds carry the whole recipe. They keep in a tin for up to two weeks and are better the day after baking, once fully dried out. Use a mix of seeds for variety in texture and flavour.
sourceNotes: Seeded crispbreads in the Scandinavian knackebrod tradition are documented from medieval Sweden and Finland onward. Thin yeasted and unyeasted flatbreads with seeds are documented across northern Europe as a staple winter food intended to be kept for months.

recipe.yieldDescription: about 20 to 24 crispbreads depending on size
recipe.batchNotes: The dough multiplies easily. Bake in batches on lined trays, swapping tray positions halfway.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 weeks. The crispbreads are better the day after baking once they have dried out fully.

content.text: Seeded crispbreads need to be rolled as thin as possible; a thick crispbread is a soft cracker, not crisp through. Aim for 2 mm or thinner. The seeds hold the dough together as it rolls and prevent it tearing. Bake until completely dry; any softness when they come out of the oven means they need more time and will be chewy once cool.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Mix the flours, salt, and seeds together in a bowl. Add the olive oil and water and mix until a stiff dough forms. It will look dry at first; keep mixing.

Divide the dough in half. Roll each piece directly on a sheet of baking paper, using the rolling pin to push the dough out very thin, about 2 mm. The seeds will cause the dough to tear; press the tears together and keep rolling. Transfer the paper and dough to the prepared trays.
Score the dough into irregular shards or rectangles using a knife or pastry cutter, but leave in place on the tray.

Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until the crispbreads are golden and completely dry. The edges will colour before the centre; if the centre is still pale, give another 3 to 5 minutes. Cool completely on the tray; they crisp further as they cool.
Break into pieces along the score lines. Store in an airtight tin.

attrs.problem: Crispbreads chewy and bendy rather than crisp
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling the dough too thick or removing the crispbreads from the oven before they are completely dry.
attrs.fix: Return the tray to the oven at a lower temperature (150 degrees C / fan 130 degrees C) for another 10 minutes to drive off the remaining moisture. They should feel completely rigid before removing.

attrs.problem: Dough tearing into pieces when rolling
attrs.avoid: Avoid working quickly; the seeds need time to embed and the dough needs to be worked gently.
attrs.fix: Press tears together firmly and roll over them again. Rolling on baking paper rather than a floured surface helps; you can lift the paper and the dough comes with it intact.
